subject.title: feat(agents): expose inbound turn identifiers to CLI subprocesses

question: Should OpenClaw expose inbound message identifiers to long-lived CLI subprocesses through a session-scoped on-disk file, and if so what retention and invalidation guarantees must that public contract provide?
rationale: The mechanical defects are fixable, but deciding whether this durable subprocess-visible metadata surface is acceptable is a security and product-boundary choice rather than a code-review preference.

options.title: Approve a bounded file contract
options.body: Retain the capability only with opaque collision-resistant paths, stale-file invalidation on write failure, restrictive permissions, and documented lifecycle semantics.

options.title: Keep identifiers prompt-only
options.body: Decline the durable file contract and preserve the existing prompt-based metadata exposure until a narrower supported integration boundary is designed.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded file contract
recommendation.body: Retain the capability only with opaque collision-resistant paths, stale-file invalidation on write failure, restrictive permissions, and documented lifecycle semantics.
